assumptions: Timing uses standard Australian statutory periods. Verify each against IP Australia before relying on it.
Convention Priority Deadline = Application Filed + 6 months (Paris Convention).
Acceptance / OA Response deadline = OA Issued + 15 months (extendable to 21 months with fees).
Opposition period expires = Publication Date (advertised accepted) + 2 months.
Renewal Deadline = Application Filed + 10 years; renewals every 10 years thereafter.
Renewal reminders assumed at 6 months, 3 months and 1 month before deadline; final reminder on the deadline; grace period 6 months after.
Non-use vulnerability = Application Filed + 5 years (earliest a removal action can be brought).
Deferment for prior use deadline = Deferment request lodged + 6 months.
Opposition proceedings assumed: SGP due = NIO filed + 1 month; NID due = SGP filed + 1 month; Evidence in Support due = NID + 3 months; cooling-off period = 6 months.
Australia no longer charges a separate registration fee (paid at filing); the Registration Fee Due rule is retained as manual/optional for legacy matters.
Headstart part-2 fee due and Divisional dates are treated as manual — no fixed statutory offset.

Applicant: [CompanyName]
Trade Mark: [TrademarkName]
Application Number: [ApplicationNumber]
Goods/Services: [GoodsServices]
Filing Date: [ApplicationFiled]

What Next?
This application will now be examined by IP Australia in around 4-6 months. If you would like examination sooner, we can request that it be expedited (additional cost of $475+GST per mark). The minimum time for a trade mark application to be registered is 7.5 months after the filing date without complication or opposition.

If objections to registration are not raised, the application will be advertised as accepted for a mandatory two month opposition period. If objections are raised, our fee to report examination is around $650 + GST.

Possible overseas applications
If you intend to use the mark overseas, it would be prudent to file overseas applications within 6 months of the Australian application, i.e. on or before [ConventionPriorityDeadline], to claim the Australian filing date under the Paris Convention.

Bogus Trade Mark Registers
We wish to draw your attention to the possibility of unsolicited requests from companies outside Australia offering to include your mark in a non-authorised register. Please do not pay any requested fees before discussing them with us.

templates.body:
USE THE BELOW FOR A NATIONAL AUSTRALIAN TRADE MARK

Dear [FirstName],

We are pleased to inform you that your trade mark is now registered in Australia. We have received the Certificate of Registration and attach the original Certificate for your files.

Registration No.: [RegistrationNumber]
Trade Mark: [TrademarkName]
Goods/Services: [GoodsServices]
Renewal Deadline: [RenewalDeadline]

The initial registration term is 10 years from the date of filing and the mark can be renewed every ten years thereafter on payment of the official renewal fees. We have made a note of the next renewal date and will advise you in advance of the renewal requirements.

Maintaining your registration:
1. Use your trade mark - if not used for a continuous period of 3 years, the registration may be subject to non-use cancellation.
2. Use the mark precisely in the form in which it is registered.
3. Use a trade mark notice - the R symbol should only be used once the mark is registered.
4. Record any change of name/title or assignment with IP Australia.
5. Watching service available on request.

USE THE BELOW FOR AN AUSTRALIAN DESIGNATION UNDER THE MADRID PROTOCOL
As this is a designation under the Madrid Protocol, you will be responsible for the renewal of the international registration. We have however made a note of the renewal deadline for the above designation in our database.

CLOSING OF OUR FILE
Now that the matter is at an end, we take this opportunity to attach our formal Archive Letter.
